parts.note: Shaw subtitled his one-act play about a horse thief acquitted after a change of heart 'a sermon in crude melodrama'; the clue echoes its title, The Shewing-Up of ...

explanation.surface: A theatre note on a hero cleared of guilt in a preachy melodrama.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A in 'A sermon' marks a quoted subtitle: George Bernard Shaw's 1909 play The Shewing-Up of Blanco Posnet, in which a horse thief is unexpectedly acquitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's title character is the man whose 'shewing-up' ends in his release, the play bearing the quoted subtitle.

parts.words: "O — Envy! thou self-tormenting fiend" (Tobias Smollett, Peregrine Pickle)

explanation.walkthrough: The dash is the gap: Smollett's line runs 'O baleful Envy! thou self-tormenting fiend'. The adjective fits as menacing and harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy that torments itself is malign and harmful, the sense of the missing adjective in Smollett's line.

explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson's comedies Every Man in His Humour (1598) and Every Man out of His Humour turn on the old theory of the humours, moods.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary typical person is the common man of the medieval morality play, and Jonson's Elizabethan comedy of humours has the same opening words.
